events.title: Church of the Holy Sepulchre Destroyed
events.description: On the orders of the Fatimid caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, the church in Jerusalem traditionally regarded as the site of Jesus's crucifixion and burial was torn down.
events.significance: The destruction shocked Christian Europe and is often cited among the grievances that helped build momentum for the later Crusades.

events.title: The United States Takes Possession of Alaska
events.description: In a formal ceremony at Sitka, Russia transferred Alaska to the United States following its purchase for $7.2 million. Alaska also moved from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar.
events.significance: The acquisition, once mocked as 'Seward's Folly', added vast natural resources and strategic territory to the U.S. The date is still celebrated in Alaska as Alaska Day.

events.title: Thomas Edison Dies
events.description: The prolific American inventor died at his home in West Orange, New Jersey, at age 84, from complications of diabetes.
events.significance: Edison's work on the phonograph, practical electric lighting and motion picture technology helped shape the modern world, and he held more than a thousand patents.

events.title: Galileo Probe Launched Toward Jupiter
events.description: NASA's Galileo spacecraft was launched on its journey to study Jupiter and its moons.
events.significance: Galileo became the first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter and delivered key discoveries, including evidence of a subsurface ocean on Europa.
